body.statement: Using \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{rob}}\), determine \(\rho_{\mathrm{eval}}(n,\epsilon;d,\alpha,\beta,\kappa,L)\) and construct \(T_n^\star\) so that, jointly for all \(n\geq2\) and \(0\leq\epsilon\leq1/10\), \[c_0\rho_{\mathrm{eval}}\leq\mathfrak R_n(\epsilon;d,\alpha,\beta,\kappa,L)\leq\sup_{(P,Q,R)\in\mathcal C_{d,\alpha,\beta,\kappa,L}(\epsilon)}\mathbb E_{R^n}|T_n^\star-\theta(P)|\leq C_0\rho_{\mathrm{eval}}.\] The rate must be an explicit finite piecewise formula with every equality-case logarithm; the estimator must be total, finite, data-only, and computationally specified; and the converse must use the same contaminated experiment. The result must decide whether the clean functional rate and \(\omega_\theta(\epsilon/(1-\epsilon))\) are simultaneously attainable or whether a quantified nuisance-contamination interaction term is unavoidable.
body.justification: This first-class open extension asks whether the simultaneous attainment proved by the one-dimensional calibration persists across the full multidimensional smoothness phase diagram.
body.gap: Section 3 of MaSantAnnaSasakiUra2026 starts from clean i.i.d. observations and Appendix B, Proposition B.1 verifies its ATE trimming and boundary-bias conditions; neither allows arbitrary replacement of \(X\), \(A\), and \(Y\). ChenGaoRen2016 gives generic Huber testing, and RobinsEtAl2017HOEE gives clean higher-order correction, but neither supplies the requested robust fast-functional construction and same-experiment Huber-neighborhood converse on this boundary class.
body.consumer: SasakiUra2022Robustate gains a theoretical error-radius and boundary-correction benchmark that separates limited-overlap robustness from unreliable-record robustness.

obligation.what_is_open: Construct a total finite data-only robust slabwise projected correction, including contaminated nuisance pilots and estimated Gram matrices, whose proved uniform error bound remains valid when the projection dimension exceeds stable local occupancy; or prove a same-class interaction lower bound showing that such preservation is impossible. The resulting bounds must then be optimized over all slabs and boundary resolutions, including every equality-case logarithm.
obligation.obstruction: The frozen handle names the desired operations but states no quantitative robustness property from which an upper bound can be derived. For the raw off-diagonal correction, a contaminant concentrated at one projected cell contributes a diagonal-sized bias of order \(\epsilon^2 K x_1^{-2\kappa}\); diffusing the contamination within that cell does not supply a law-independent cancellation. Coordinatewise robustification of pilots and Gram entries does not control the many pairwise terms when local clean occupancy is below \(K\), while truncating to stable occupancy can erase the clean high-resolution functional gain. No frozen result supplies either a robust replacement inequality or a lower-bound construction certifying the resulting interaction term.
obligation.attempted: The exact projected nuisance-product identity was expanded under both a point contaminant and contamination diffuse within one fine cell. The clean degeneracy removes first-order pilot bias, but the contaminated Hoeffding expectation retains the \(\epsilon^2\)-weighted kernel diagonal. Bounding individual moments by their ranges yields a tuning-dependent term growing with projection dimension and inverse overlap; clipping it to the TV-modulus scale forces a resolution below that needed for the proposed fast clean correction. Conversely, this failure is estimator-specific because an atom or an anomalous cell may be filtered, so it cannot be promoted to a minimax interaction lower bound.
obligation.partial_result:
The proved same-experiment facts imply, uniformly for \(0<\epsilon\leq1/10\),
\[
 \mathfrak R_n(\epsilon;d,\alpha,\beta,\kappa,L)
 \geq \mathfrak R_n(0;d,\alpha,\beta,\kappa,L)
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 \mathfrak R_n(\epsilon;d,\alpha,\beta,\kappa,L)
 \geq c\left(\frac{\epsilon}{1-\epsilon}\right)^{(\beta+1)/(\beta+\kappa+1)}.
\]
The first inequality follows by taking \(Q=P\).  For the second, use the bump pair in the proof of \(\texttt{thm:ate-tv-modulus}\), choose its total variation at most \(\epsilon/(1-\epsilon)\), and apply the explicit Jordan-decomposition collision calculation from \(\texttt{lem:lipschitz-lower-pair}\); the two observed laws then coincide and pointwise triangle inequality gives half the target separation.  For \(\epsilon/(1-\epsilon)\leq\delta_0\), choose equality in the total-variation constraint.  Above that threshold, retain the fixed pair at radius \(\delta_0\) and decrease the constant, which is legitimate because \(\epsilon\leq1/10\).  Moreover, when \((d,\alpha,\beta,\kappa)=(1,1,1,2)\), \(\texttt{thm:lipschitz-calibration}\) proves the complete matched rate \(n^{-2/5}+\epsilon^{1/2}\), so simultaneous attainment is established in that regime.  No corresponding general upper bound or matching interaction lower bound has been derived.
